A variety of methods are used in [[econometrics]] to '''estimate [[model (economics)|models]] consisting of a single [[equation]]'''. The oldest and still the most commonly used is the [[ordinary least squares]] method used to estimate [[linear regression]]s.<ref name="koutsoyiannis1973">{{Cite book |last=Koutsoyiannis |first=A. |url=https://archive.org/details/theoryofeconomet0000kout/page/48/mode/1up?q=%22ordinary+least+squares%22 |title=Theory of econometrics: an introductory exposition of econometric methods |date=1973 |publisher=Harper & Row |isbn=978-0-06-493950-8 |location=New York |pages=48 |language=en}}</ref>

A variety of methods are available to estimate [[non-linear]] models. A particularly important class of non-linear models are those used to estimate relationships where the [[dependent variable]] is discrete, [[Truncated dependent variable|truncated]] or censored. These include [[logit]], [[probit]] and [[Tobit model|Tobit]] models. 

Single equation methods may be applied to [[time-series]], cross section or panel data.
